question: The term ‘chui’ in judo means ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**light penalty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The term 'chui' in judo is used to denote a **light penalty**.
 
• It is one of the penalties given for minor infringements of the rules during a judo match.
 
• Receiving multiple 'chui' penalties can lead to more severe penalties or disqualification.
 
• This penalty system is designed to ensure fair play and adherence to the rules of the sport.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shido**

 
 
• It is another type of light penalty in judo, often given for minor rule violations.
 
• Accumulating several shido penalties can result in more serious consequences.
 
 
 
• **Hansoku-make**
 
 
• This is the most severe penalty in judo and leads to disqualification from the match.
 
• It is given for serious rule violations or unsportsmanlike behavior.
 
 
 
• **Judo Scoring System**
 
 
• Points in judo are awarded based on the effectiveness of throws, holds, and submissions.
 
• The main scoring terms are Ippon, Waza-ari, and Yuko.
 
 
 
• **Judo Techniques**
 
 
• Judo techniques are classified into throws (nage-waza), holds (osaekomi-waza), and submissions (shime-waza and kansetsu-waza).
 
• Each technique has specific rules and guidelines for proper execution.
